current.text: He signed a minimum contract to return to Orlando as a backup.
Wendell Carter Jr. is Orlando's starting center and Vucevic is his backup. Goga Bitadze will also get some center minutes.

Experts expect fewer minutes than his 28 last season, but they disagree on how many: one sees 20 to 22 minutes, another sees 15 to 20 and does not expect him to push for a starting role. One expert says he could even be third string.
Orlando added him to fix a bench that ranked 27th or 28th in scoring. He is expected to score 12 to 14 points a game off the bench and to be an upgrade on Mo Wagner.
His value rises a lot if Wendell Carter Jr. gets hurt. He could then be a top 100 player.
Experts agree it is a mistake to draft him as a starter or at his ESPN ADP. At most he is a late flyer, worth a pick only in deep drafts.
Lloyd will not draft him. He says Vucevic is cooked.
His assists got a lift from luck last season, with a 68% potential assist conversion rate, so they may drop.
Orlando has a new head coach, Sean Sweeney, who replaces Jamahl Mosley. Player roles may change.

durable.text: He is a pretty good passer for a big man.
He gets rebounds without blocking shots. He is the exception to the rule that rebounders also block shots.
His steals are weak for a center, so a punt STL team loses little with him.

note: He went for 17 USD in our league last season. Now he is a bench center behind Wendell Carter Jr., with a Yahoo value of 0 USD and an ESPN value of 2 USD, so pay 1 to 2 USD at most, and only as a late flyer or Carter handcuff. If you take him, he fits a punt STL build. Early in the season, check his minutes under new coach Sean Sweeney, how much Goga Bitadze plays, and Carter's health.
